messages.author: e04bb64c7c0b4424
messages.subject: Workarounds for Shiny upload limits
parts:
I am trying to work with csv files that contain big data. Most of the files are about 4 columns and 400,000+ rows. With smaller data sets my application is able to successfully plot the information but with the larger files it is not even uploading the files.

The point of the application is to dynamically choose csv files containing big data so that the user can analyse them.  I realize the Shiny has a 5 megabyte upload limit which can be changed to 30 megabytes but is there a way to bypass this with a dynamic database, streaming, or anything else?  I know that I could pre-load a file with a global variable outside of the shiny server but I am trying to make the application dynamic.

messages.author: e84e7628b5f8a3e1
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Workarounds for Shiny upload limits
parts:
How large are the files you are attempting to upload? I believe the limit can be increased up to around 100MB, but I would need to double check that. However, I would not recommending planning to upload files that large. In my opinion the performance would be too slow, and offer a poor user experience.

If you're looking for alternate means, have you considering storing your data in a database such as Amazon RDS?

-Andy
